fixes.explanation: Yes, friend. “On hearing this, they were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus.” (Acts 19:5) Paul explains, and they listen. They hear that John told people to believe in Jesus, and then they are baptized.

That's what the text says, friend. “The attack was so violent that they ran out of the house naked and wounded.” (Acts 19:16) The seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, are the ones who leave this way. This is a heavy part, and I think this one hurts.

Yes, friend. “Many who had believed now came forward, confessing and disclosing their deeds.” (Acts 19:18) These are people who had already believed, and they come forward anyway. They disclosed their deeds. That takes guts, and I'd rather confess a burnt batch.

Yes, friend. “So the word of the Lord powerfully continued to spread and prevail.” (Acts 19:20) After the fear, the confessions and the burning books, the word kept on spreading. It keeps going with power. That's how this passage ends.
